heading: Massachusetts Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Massachusetts paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Massachusetts income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable Paid Family and Medical Leave contributions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, choose your payment frequency and customize your payroll deductions to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Massachusetts applies a standard income tax rate to ordinary wages, but higher-income employees may also encounter an additional surtax. Paid family and medical leave contributions can further affect take-home earnings.

Whether you work in Boston, Cambridge, Worcester, Springfield or another Massachusetts community, understanding these deductions can help you compare employment opportunities and manage your finances.

## How to Use the Massachusetts Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your earnings before taxes and deductions, then choose your payment frequency.

Enter federal and Massachusetts income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub. Include any surtax already withheld in the Massachusetts total.

Include retirement contributions and health insurance premiums. If Massachusetts paid leave contributions were withheld, enter those amounts under Benefits in Advanced settings, under Other deductions.

Enter prior year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching a Social Security or Additional Medicare threshold.

Review your estimated gross pay, individual deductions and remaining take-home income.

Use your latest pay stub and withholding certificates for greater accuracy.

## Massachusetts Payroll Taxes in 2026

Massachusetts employees may encounter the following payroll deductions.

The exact amount deducted depends on your earnings, withholding elections, employer contribution arrangements and employee benefits.

Visit the [Massachusetts Department of Revenue tax rates page](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/tax-rates) for official information.

## How Massachusetts State Income Tax Works

Massachusetts generally applies a 5% individual income tax rate to ordinary employment earnings.

However, this rate should not automatically be multiplied by your entire gross salary when calculating paycheck withholding.

Employers account for the applicable withholding exemptions and authorized payroll adjustments.

Massachusetts publishes Circular M, which contains the state's employer income tax withholding tables and percentage calculation methods.

Employees receiving identical gross salaries may have different Massachusetts withholding amounts because of differences in personal exemptions, benefit arrangements or additional withholding requests.

Review the official [Massachusetts withholding tax forms and Circular M](https://www.mass.gov/lists/withholding-tax-forms) to understand the applicable calculation procedures.

## Massachusetts High-Income Surtax in 2026

Massachusetts introduced an additional 4% surtax on taxable income above an annually adjusted threshold beginning in 2023.

The 2026 threshold is $1,107,750.

Only the portion of applicable taxable income exceeding the threshold is subject to the additional 4%.

For example, suppose an individual has $1,200,000 in annual taxable income subject to the surtax calculation.

Income above the threshold:

$1,200,000 − $1,107,750 = $92,250

Additional annual surtax:

$92,250 × 4% = $3,690

This example illustrates annual surtax liability rather than an individual paycheck calculation.

Employers must use the applicable wage withholding rules, which may differ from the final annual tax calculation when employees have multiple jobs or other income.

Read the official [Massachusetts 4% surtax guidance](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/massachusetts-4-surtax-on-taxable-income) for further information.

## Understanding Massachusetts Form M-4

Massachusetts employees generally use Form M-4, the Employee's Withholding Exemption Certificate, to communicate state withholding information to their employers.

The form allows employees to claim applicable exemptions and request additional withholding.

Massachusetts withholding selections are separate from federal Form W-4 adjustments.

Review your M-4 information when starting employment, getting married, experiencing changes in household circumstances or determining that your current withholding is insufficient.

Claiming additional exemptions can affect the amount withheld from your paycheck. However, it does not automatically reduce your final annual income tax liability.

Current employee withholding forms are available from the Massachusetts Department of Revenue.

## Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave Contributions

Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave, commonly called PFML, provides qualifying workers with temporary income replacement during eligible periods of leave.

For employers with at least 25 covered individuals, the standard combined public program contribution rate is 0.88% in 2026.

The employee and employer may share the contribution.

Employers may voluntarily cover some or all of the employee contribution.

## Massachusetts PFML Deduction Examples

Assuming the full 0.46% employee contribution applies and the annual covered wage ceiling has not been reached:

The applicable annual wage ceiling corresponds to the Social Security wage limit, which is $184,500 in 2026.

At the full 0.46% employee contribution rate, the maximum standard annual contribution is $848.70.

Private insurance plans, employer-paid arrangements and certain employment classifications may produce different deductions.

Consult the [Massachusetts PFML contribution guidance](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/paid-family-and-medical-leave-employer-contribution-rates-and-calculator) for official rates and employer cost-sharing requirements.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Massachusetts Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable earnings, filing status, payment frequency and Form W-4 information.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered wages, subject to an annual taxable wage ceiling of $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered earnings without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% once Medicare-covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [federal withholding calculation instructions](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) for additional information.

Consider an employee earning $78,000 annually before taxes and deductions.
Assume the employee receives $3,000 biweekly and is subject to ordinary federal payroll contributions and the maximum standard employee PFML contribution.

Approximately $2,756.70 remains before federal income tax, Massachusetts income tax and other employee deductions.

This example illustrates selected payroll contributions rather than a complete net paycheck calculation.

Use your actual withholding information and benefit deductions to estimate your final take-home income.

## Massachusetts Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can calculate their gross earnings using their wage and qualifying working hours.

For example, suppose an employee earns $32 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus five qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$32 × 40 = $1,280

Overtime earnings:

$32 × 1.5 × 5 = $240

Total gross earnings:

$1,520

Federal taxes, Massachusetts income tax and applicable paid leave contributions are then calculated from their respective taxable wage amounts.

Overtime eligibility depends on employment classification and applicable state and federal labor requirements.

Consult the [Massachusetts overtime guidance](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/massachusetts-law-about-overtime) for more information.

## Does Boston Have a Local Income Tax?

Boston generally does not impose a separate municipal personal wage income tax.

Employees working in Boston are still subject to applicable Massachusetts and federal income taxes and payroll contributions.

However, housing, transportation and other living expenses can differ considerably between Boston, Cambridge and other Massachusetts communities.

When comparing employment opportunities, calculate your estimated net income first and then evaluate local living costs separately.

## Working in Massachusetts and Living in New Hampshire

Many employees living in southern New Hampshire commute to Massachusetts for employment.

Although New Hampshire does not impose individual income tax on ordinary wages, Massachusetts may tax qualifying employment earnings sourced to Massachusetts.

Employees working remotely or performing employment duties across state borders may need additional income allocation calculations.

Do not assume that living in New Hampshire automatically eliminates Massachusetts withholding.

Consult the Massachusetts Department of Revenue for guidance on nonresident income taxation.

## Planning Your Massachusetts Monthly Budget

Compare job offers using estimated take-home income rather than gross annual salary alone.

Include housing, transportation, healthcare premiums and other recurring expenses when establishing spending limits.

Employees working in the Boston metropolitan area may find that housing and commuting expenses substantially influence the practical value of their salaries.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a suitable savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare fixed salaries with hourly employment.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the Massachusetts income tax rate in 2026?

Massachusetts generally applies a 5% rate to ordinary wage income. An additional 4% surtax applies to qualifying taxable income exceeding $1,107,750 in 2026.

### How much is Massachusetts PFML deducted from paychecks?

The maximum standard employee contribution in 2026 is generally 0.46% of covered wages, consisting of family leave and medical leave contributions.

### Does Boston have a separate employee income tax?

Boston generally does not impose a separate municipal personal wage income tax. Applicable Massachusetts and federal payroll deductions still apply.
